items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: Baby Dodds used to talk about it too. Most of the New Orleans bands would follow.

ctx.x: So you researched the King Oliver chapter?

Partly. I wouldn't say that. Just the people in Chicago. Right. Because after all, Oliver did most of his important recording and you might say later playing in Chicago. So a lot of people there knew him and several members of the band were still living like, of course, Lil and Louie. And Bill Johnson, Dodds, both the Dodds brothers. So Ramsey couldn't get away from his job at Harcourt. So I did that work for him. All that we could. Unfortunately, no tape machines then. Just had to do it longhand. And I'd take…
Was Steve Smith's wife really interested and involved in things?

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: When I first met Johnny Dodds about 1936, I went to Chicago and I inquired if he was playing anyplace or where he was.

ctx.x: 1949. It says here she was approximately later, 11 years older than George Bakke. I figured that out. To get on to a few other people that I used to talk to, the next one on this list was Johnny Dodds, whose notes I'll have to send. They probably are in a box of Baby Dodds notes, I think. I was always going to try to rewrite them. When I first met Johnny Dodds about 1936, I went to Chicago and I inquired if he was playing anyplace or where he was. All I knew about him, he'd been on some of the jelly roll records…

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-08-31
items.q: So up there in Chicago I'd interviewed Baby Dodds quite a few interviews, as well as some of his music, demonstrating the drums and different traps as they call them.

ctx.x: Well, you think that maybe it has something to do with the general environment.

Or else it's the type of people that, for one thing, one of the great principles which you can't really overemphasize in New Orleans music, in the jazz, is the working together. The way they can work together. They're all there to help one another, as they say. They'll, they're not there to steal the spotlight. They're always there trying to help somebody misses a note or they can see they're falling down on their part. They'll put in notes that'll fill in or they'll, I mean, it's not quite that simple, but I…
He was my favorite of all of them on my own record.
